promises.title: You own it
promises.line: Your site is a GitHub repository in your name, with its full history. Nothing of yours stays with us.
promises.proof: We expect every site we build to move into its owner's ownership within three months: the repository transferred to your GitHub account and the address pointed where you choose. It is an expectation today, not yet a rule we enforce.

promises.title: Nobody can lock you in
promises.line: No platform, no subscription, no terms but yours. The code is open source, so nobody can withdraw it, us included.
promises.proof: Sovereignty is not where a site is hosted. It is whether you can move the site, its data and its structure somewhere else, and you can.

promises.title: You change it by talking to Claude
promises.line: Ask your own Claude for a change in plain words. A behaviour policy and checks run before anything goes live, and every change can be undone.
promises.proof: Yiheng Wang gave Claude her CV as a PDF; Claude read it and added her latest experience to her site.

promises.title: You can run it anywhere
promises.line: The site is static files. They run on GitHub Pages for free, or on any web host, in any region you choose.
promises.proof: Each host's own instructions for putting the site online, linked from one page.

promises.title: It looks better
promises.line: A team of agents makes five designs from your material and the sites you like. You choose one, and the others are kept.
promises.proof: The sites we have already made, each labelled as a named person's site or a demo.

promises.title: Almost nothing to attack, and it costs once
promises.line: No server code, no database, no plugins, no cookies unless you add them. One payment instead of a monthly bill.
promises.proof: Why a static site in your own repository is an alternative to WordPress, Wix and Squarespace, with the vendors' own security figures labelled as theirs.

deliverables.name: A GitHub repository in your name

deliverables.why_it_matters: It is the site. Whoever holds the repository holds the site, and that is you.

deliverables.name: A live site, with HTTPS
deliverables.what: Your site online at its address, on your own domain if you have one.
deliverables.why_it_matters: It works from the first day, and the address is yours to point wherever you choose.

deliverables.why_it_matters: It is easier to point at a design you like than to describe one. You can switch later.

deliverables.why_it_matters: Your own Claude can change the site safely from the first conversation.

deliverables.name: A behaviour policy and checks

deliverables.why_it_matters: A change that would break the site or publish something private is stopped before it is public.

deliverables.name: Ownership within three months

deliverables.why_it_matters: We hold the site only to finish the work. After that we hold nothing, so there is nothing to stop paying for.

steps.title: The interview
steps.line: Claude interviews you: what the site is for, the sections you want, the material you have, three sites you like and why, and what must stay private. The answers become a one-page brief, in your words.

steps.title: Five designs
steps.line: A team of agents makes five designs from your material, inspired by the qualities you named in the sites you like, never copies of them.

steps.title: You choose
steps.line: You pick one design, or ask for parts of two. You say what to change.

steps.title: Live
steps.line: The site goes live at its address, with HTTPS, after the checks pass.

steps.title: Your first change, made together
steps.line: You ask your own Claude for a change, it goes live, and we both see it. This is the moment you have what we sell.

steps.title: Hand-over
steps.line: The repository moves to your GitHub account, within three months at the latest. From then on we hold nothing.

sections.honest_notes: Two things you should know before you buy.

faq.a: {launch} once, at the [launch price](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-sovereign-website.html), usually {usual}. There is no subscription from us. Hosting on GitHub Pages is free, and editing needs your own Claude plan or a partner.

faq.q: Can I see one before I pay?
faq.a: Yes. We build a limited number of sites each day free of charge, for evaluation. [Ask for a site]({{contact}}) and say you would like a free evaluation.

You do. It is a GitHub repository in your name, with its full history. We expect every site to move into its owner's ownership within three months at the latest; that is an expectation today, not yet a rule we enforce ([the reasoning](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/fliplet-and-the-website-cell.html)).

faq.q: Can I move it to another host?
faq.a: Yes, whenever you like. The site is static files, so it runs on GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel or any web host. [Put your site online](https://agenticcells.ai/deploy/) links to each host's own instructions.

faq.q: What if you disappear, or are bought?
faq.a: Nothing changes for you. You already hold the files, their history and the instructions for your Claude, and the code is open source, so nobody can withdraw it ([sovereignty you can move](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/sovereignty-you-can-move.html)).

faq.q: Do I need a GitHub account?
faq.a: Yes, to receive the repository at hand-over. Making one is free, and we point you to the guidance. Until then the site runs on our account so we can finish the work.

faq.q: How do I change the site later?
faq.a: Tell your own Claude what you want, in plain words: a new page, a new photo, your latest job from a CV. The site's CLAUDE.md and behaviour policy tell Claude how to do it safely, the checks run before anything goes live, and any change can be undone. You need a Claude plan for this, or a partner who edits it for you.

Every change is a commit, so any version can be restored. The checks stop most broken or private changes before they go live. A static site is not automatically safe, though: if you want a person to watch over it, a partner can sell you that.
You, with your own Claude, or a partner you choose. We sell no subscription and no support: our part ends when the site is yours.

faq.q: Can I use my own domain?
faq.a: Yes. The site can run on your own domain with HTTPS. Until you have one, it runs on an address of ours. The domain stays registered in your name, with the registrar you choose.

The agents write in your language, and a site can carry more than one. This site's own pages are written in several languages; the translations are made by agents and say so until a native speaker checks them.

There is very little to attack: no server code, no database, no plugins, no login page on the site, and no cookies unless you add them. What it does not protect is your GitHub account and your domain registrar: keep both behind two-factor sign-in. The [security page](/next/security/) says more.

Freelancers, consultancies and firms who sell the site to their customers while we build it. The customer still owns the site; the partner keeps the relationship and may sell hosting, care and changes at their own prices. [The partner terms](https://agenticcells.ai/partners/) are published.

By then the repository should be in your GitHub account and the address pointed where you choose, and we hold nothing. If you asked sooner, it happened sooner. It is an expectation today, not yet a rule we enforce.

faq.q: What if I want more than a website?
faq.a: There are two bigger offers, both first proposals: a few sessions with a person, then you run the team in your own accounts; or a team of agents set up in your accounts. The [pricing page](/next/pricing/) has both.
No. Nothing has been sold yet, and we will say so until it changes. The examples are sites made by the same team, each labelled as a named person's site or a demo.
